symbols.name: announce
symbols.summary: Announce `message` to screen readers through a live region (polite by default).
symbols.remarks:
Announce `message` to screen readers through a live region (polite by default). Live regions must
exist before their content changes: render `<Announcer/>` (`@rivetjs/cdk/announcer`) in the layout so
the first announcement is not lost; without it the regions are created on first use. The text is
cleared and set after a tick, so repeating a message announces it again. Browser only.

symbols.name: Signal
symbols.summary: A callable reactive getter with explicit write operations.
symbols.remarks:
A callable reactive getter with explicit write operations. Invariant in `T` (`set`/`update` are function
properties, checked contravariantly): a `Signal<"a" | "b">` is not a `Signal<string>`; pass the getter
(`() => string`) to read-only consumers. Both need `this` = the signal at run time (call them on it, or
bind them); the type does not model `this`, so a `Signal<A> | Signal<B>` union stays callable.

symbols.remarks:
A pending copy-to-clipboard operation. Copying modifies the DOM and forces a re-layout, which for a
large string can take long enough that the browser refuses `execCommand("copy")`: this object lets
the re-layout happen in a separate tick from copying. Call `destroy()` when done, whether or not
`copy()` was called.

symbols.remarks:
`[cdkCopyToClipboard]` click behaviour: copies `options.text`, retrying up to `attempts` times
(1 ms apart) when the browser refuses, then calls `copied(successful)` once. `owner` identifies the
trigger (usually `event.currentTarget`), so `destroyCopyToClipboard(owner)` can cancel retries.

symbols.name: IslamicCivilCalendar
symbols.summary: The Islamic calendar, also known as the "Hijri" calendar, is used throughout much of the Arab world.
symbols.remarks:
The Islamic calendar, also known as the "Hijri" calendar, is used throughout much of the Arab
world. The civil variant uses simple arithmetic rules rather than astronomical calculations to
approximate the traditional calendar, which is based on sighting of the crescent moon. It uses
Friday, July 16 622 CE (Julian) as the epoch. Each year has 12 months, with either 354 or 355
days depending on whether it is a leap year. Learn more about the available Islamic calendars
[here](https://cldr.unicode.org/development/development-process/design-proposals/islamic-calendar-types).

world. The Umalqura variant is primarily used in Saudi Arabia. It is a lunar calendar, based on
astronomical calculations that predict the sighting of a crescent moon. Month and year lengths
vary between years depending on these calculations. Learn more about the available Islamic
calendars

symbols.summary: The Japanese calendar is based on the Gregorian calendar, but with eras for the reign of each Japanese emperor.
symbols.remarks:
The Japanese calendar is based on the Gregorian calendar, but with eras for the reign of each
Japanese emperor. Whenever a new emperor ascends to the throne, a new era begins and the year
starts again from 1. Note that eras before 1868 (Gregorian) are not currently supported by this
implementation.

symbols.name: PersianCalendar
symbols.summary: The Persian calendar is the main calendar used in Iran and Afghanistan.
symbols.remarks:
The Persian calendar is the main calendar used in Iran and Afghanistan. It has 12 months
in each year, the first 6 of which have 31 days, and the next 5 have 30 days. The 12th month
has either 29 or 30 days depending on whether it is a leap year. The Persian year starts
around the March equinox.

members.name: previewContainer
members.doc:
Configures the place into which the preview of the item will be inserted. Can be configured
globally through `DragDropConfigContext`. Possible values:
- `global` - Preview will be inserted at the bottom of the `<body>`. The advantage is that
you don't have to worry about `overflow: hidden` or `z-index`, but the item won't retain
its inherited styles.
- `parent` - Preview will be inserted into the parent of the drag item. The advantage is that
inherited styles will be preserved, but it may be clipped by `overflow: hidden` or not be
visible due to `z-index`. Furthermore, the preview is going to have an effect over selectors
like `:nth-child` and some flexbox configurations.
- `ElementLike` - Preview will be inserted into a specific element.
Same advantages and disadvantages as `parent`.

members.name: previewContainer
members.doc:
Configures the place into which the preview of the item will be inserted. Can be configured
globally through `DragDropConfigContext`. Possible values:
- `global` - Preview will be inserted at the bottom of the `<body>`. The advantage is that
you don't have to worry about `overflow: hidden` or `z-index`, but the item won't retain
its inherited styles.
- `parent` - Preview will be inserted into the parent of the drag item. The advantage is that
inherited styles will be preserved, but it may be clipped by `overflow: hidden` or not be
visible due to `z-index`. Furthermore, the preview is going to have an effect over selectors
like `:nth-child` and some flexbox configurations.
- `ElementLike` - Preview will be inserted into a specific element.
Same advantages and disadvantages as `parent`.

Possible places into which the preview of a drag item can be inserted.

you don't have to worry about `overflow: hidden` or `z-index`, but the item won't retain
its inherited styles.

inherited styles will be preserved, but it may be clipped by `overflow: hidden` or not be
visible due to `z-index`. Furthermore, the preview is going to have an effect over selectors
like `:nth-child` and some flexbox configurations.
- `ElementLike` - Preview will be inserted into a specific element.
Same advantages and disadvantages as `parent`.

Whether pressing the escape key to close the popover should be disabled.

Most popovers should not use this option. When set to true, an alternative
way to close the popover with a keyboard must be provided.

members.doc:
Whether the popover is non-modal, i.e. elements outside the popover may be
interacted with by assistive technologies.

Most popovers should not use this option as it may negatively impact the screen
reader experience. Only use with components such as combobox, which are designed
to handle this situation carefully.

not reach buttons inside the overlay.

members.name: resize
members.doc:
Update the Panel's size.

Size can be in the following formats:
- Percentage of the parent Group (0..100)
- Pixels
- Relative font units (em, rem)
- Viewport relative units (vh, vw)

ℹ️ Numeric values are assumed to be pixels.
Strings without explicit units are assumed to be percentages (0%..100%).
Percentages may also be specified as strings ending with "%" (e.g. "33%")
Pixels may also be specified as strings ending with the unit "px".

symbols.name: SchedulerOffsetBound
symbols.summary: What the caller does with the minutes `minutesFromOffset` returns.
symbols.remarks:
What the caller does with the minutes `minutesFromOffset` returns.

- `'end'` — an edge. `maxMinutes` is legal: an event may end at the window's close, midnight included.
- `'start'` — the start of a slot or of a dropped event. `maxMinutes` is **not** legal there: no slot starts at
  the window's close, and a start of `MINUTES_PER_DAY` rolls onto the next day. The ceiling drops one snap step
  below `maxMinutes`.

symbols.name: assignLanes
symbols.summary: First-fit lane packing.
symbols.remarks:
First-fit lane packing. Segments are ordered by first day, then by **descending** span (the longest bar in a row
takes the top lane), then all-day before timed, then by start time, then by event id — so the result is
deterministic for any input order. The returned array is in that order, not the input's; the input is left
untouched.

symbols.name: clusterColumns
symbols.summary: Sweep-line overlap clustering per day column.
symbols.remarks:
Sweep-line overlap clustering per day column. Touching segments do not overlap.

Drag-preview ghosts (`normalized.ghost`) take no part in the packing and are appended last with `column: 0,
columns: 1` — full width, over their siblings — so a preview never resizes the events it is dragged across, and
the event being dragged keeps the geometry it had before the drag started.

(all-day = midnight). A wall time in a DST gap resolves `"compatible"` (later).

The weekday indices in `hiddenDays` that can actually hide a rendered day: `dayOfWeek` only ever returns an
integer `0`–`6`, so anything else is dropped. A set covering **every** weekday is ignored rather than rendering
an empty grid — `visibleDays`, `rowLength`, `nextVisibleDate` and the month keyboard handler share this repair so
they can never disagree about how wide a week row is or which columns exist.

symbols.name: layoutRow
symbols.summary: Applies a per-row lane budget.
symbols.remarks:
Applies a per-row lane budget. When the row needs more lanes than `visibleLanes`, the last visible lane is given
to the "+N more" button, so lanes `>= visibleLanes − 1` are hidden everywhere in the row.

Precondition: `segments` carries the `lane` numbers `assignLanes` produced for **one** row — the budget is applied
per row, and `hiddenByDay` is keyed by day index within that row. A `visibleLanes` of `1` or less hides
everything, leaving the row to its "+N more" button alone.

symbols.summary: Maps a block offset inside a time column to snapped minutes of day.
symbols.remarks:
Maps a block offset inside a time column to snapped minutes of day. `offsetPx` is measured from the column's
block-start edge; the column spans `[minMinutes, maxMinutes)` over `heightPx`.

Snapping is relative to `minMinutes`, not to midnight, so an unaligned window (`08:15`–`18:15`) still snaps onto
its own slot boundaries. Aligned windows are unaffected.

symbols.remarks:
A parent's generated id that a part may replace with its own (RA `useId` + `mergeIds`): an Autocomplete's
collection id / a ComboBox's listbox id passed in a context value (`{ id: mergedId }`). When the consuming part
(`contextProps`) has its own `id`, `current` switches to it (RA re-renders the `useId` holder with the merged id),
so the parent's `aria-controls` / `aria-activedescendant` bindings follow. Runs during the part's render: on the
server that precedes the parent's attribute writes (spread accessors are written after the synchronous tree is
built), so SSR markup already points at the part's id. Plain data + a signal: serializes in context values.

symbols.name: SlotId
symbols.summary: An id for a slotted part that may not render (RA `useSlotId`).
symbols.remarks:
An id for a slotted part that may not render (RA `useSlotId`). Client render: `rendered()` starts `true` (RA's
first render keeps the id), then a `clientEffect` after mount checks `document.getElementById(id)` and drops the
id when no element has it; the check re-runs when the signals read by `deps` change (RA `depArray`). Fast path
(same semantics): a part consuming the id through `contextProps` sets `rendered` true while mounted and false when
it unmounts.
Server render (UI-COLD 2026-10-08): no check effect, so a resumed page does not boot the runtime for it.
`rendered()` starts `false` and the consuming part marks it (no server cleanup), so the serialized flag says
whether the part is in the HTML; only a server-rendered part of an id with `deps` (it may unmount later) records
its unmount cleanup as a client effect. `slotIdRef` keeps an id whose part may still render later in the tree
(RA's server HTML) and reads the flag, so the owner's binding resumes and follows the part.
Deviation from RA (which drops an id without element after mount): a server id whose part never rendered (no
`deps`) stays in the owner's attribute until that binding re-runs for another reason (a validity change, the part
mounting); assistive technology ignores IDREFs without an element. A check effect at the first interaction was
tried and dropped: it loaded the owners' chunks mid-interaction (lost DateField keys).
Plain data + a signal, so it serializes in context values.
Usage: provide `{ id: slotId }` in the part's context and read `slotIdRef(slotId)` inside the owner's
`aria-labelledby` / `-describedby` binding.

members.name: id
members.doc: The element id the part gets.

members.name: rendered
members.doc:
Whether the id is in use (an element with it exists, or it has not been checked yet); a string when the part
rendered with its own `id` prop (RA mergeIds): the id the owner must reference instead of `id`.

symbols.name: spinButtonTextValue
symbols.summary: Replace Unicode hyphen-minus (U+002D) with minus sign (U+2212).
symbols.remarks:
Replace Unicode hyphen-minus (U+002D) with minus sign (U+2212).
This ensures that macOS VoiceOver announces it as "minus" even with other characters between the minus sign
and the number (e.g. currency symbol). Otherwise it announces nothing because it assumes the character is a hyphen.
In addition, replace the empty string with the word "Empty" so that iOS VoiceOver does not read "50%" for an empty field.

symbols.name: visibleStart
symbols.summary: First visible date.
symbols.remarks:
First visible date. Rivet (resume): every focus write inside the calendar keeps `start` corrected
(`syncStart`), so an uncontrolled focus reads `start` only; a `focusedValue` signal may be written from
outside, so it reads the corrected start (`start`, `focused`). On a resumed page a binding wakes on the
first change of any signal it read on the server (not the computed it read through): the grid rows,
weekday header and page buttons depending on `focused` would be re-created on the first focus move /
range anchor, replacing the focused cell.

symbols.name: IncompleteDate
symbols.summary: This class represents a date that is incomplete or otherwise invalid as a result of user editing.
symbols.remarks:
This class represents a date that is incomplete or otherwise invalid as a result of user editing.
For example, it can represent temporary dates such as February 31st if the user edits the day
before the month. Times are represented according to an hour cycle rather than always in 24 hour
time. This enables the user to adjust the day period (e.g. am/pm) independently from the hour.

symbols.name: StepperSemantics
symbols.summary: ARIA pattern of the stepper (Rivet).
symbols.remarks:
ARIA pattern of the stepper (Rivet). `"tabs"` (default, Angular Material's accessible stepper): the header strip is a
`tablist`, headers are `tab`s with roving tabindex + arrow keys (horizontal) or `button`s with `aria-expanded` /
`aria-current="step"` (vertical), panels `tabpanel` / `region`. `"list"`: an ordered list (`ol` / `li`) with
`aria-current="step"`; interactive headers are native buttons in the Tab order (progress indicators without panels).
